headline: Meta's Shift: Facebook and WhatsApp may require payment for use
summary: The tech giant is introducing subscription models to monetize its platforms, sparking debate over free access to social media.
details: Meta is exploring the introduction of subscription-based models for its popular platforms, including Facebook and WhatsApp, moving away from its traditionally free-to-use model.
This shift is part of a broader strategy to diversify revenue streams beyond advertising, as the company faces increasing pressure to monetize its services more effectively.
While the company has already tested subscription options in some regions, a wider rollout could change how millions of users interact with their digital social networks.
Industry analysts suggest that this move could impact user growth in developing markets where free access is a primary driver of adoption.

Meta has not yet provided a specific global timeline or pricing for these potential subscriptions, but the trend points toward a 'freemium' model where basic services remain free while premium features are paid.

headline: Education Board: Urgent instructions for HSC exams issued
summary: The education board has released critical guidelines for students appearing in the Higher Secondary Certificate examinations.
details: The education board has issued urgent instructions for students appearing in the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations.
These guidelines are intended to ensure the smooth conduct of the exams and provide clarity on rules and regulations for candidates.
Students are advised to carefully review the latest directives to avoid any complications during the examination process.
The board has emphasized strict adherence to these instructions to maintain the integrity and discipline of the exam centers.
caption:
Attention HSC candidates! The education board has just released urgent instructions for your exams.

The education board has issued urgent instructions for students appearing in the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations.

These guidelines are intended to ensure the smooth conduct of the exams and provide clarity on rules and regulations for candidates.

Students are advised to carefully review the latest directives to avoid any complications during the examination process.

The board has emphasized strict adherence to these instructions to maintain the integrity and discipline of the exam centers.
